terms.definition: The point of an orbit around Earth that is farthest from Earth.

terms.name: delta-v
terms.definition: Change in velocity, written Δv: how much a spacecraft can change its motion, the currency of every mission plan, in km/s.

terms.name: descent
terms.definition: The way down to a surface, from orbit or from the atmosphere to touchdown.

terms.name: docking
terms.definition: Joining two spacecraft mechanically so that crew or cargo can pass between them.

terms.name: entry
terms.definition: A spacecraft's passage into a planet's atmosphere, where drag and heating slow it down.

terms.name: flyby
terms.definition: A close pass by a planet, moon or other body without going into orbit around it or landing.

terms.name: gravity assist
terms.definition: Using a close pass of a planet to change a spacecraft's speed and direction without spending propellant.

terms.name: inclination
terms.definition: The tilt of an orbit's plane against a reference plane, such as Earth's equator or the ecliptic, in degrees.

terms.name: orbit

terms.name: orbit insertion
terms.definition: The engine burn that slows a spacecraft enough to be captured into orbit around its destination.

terms.name: payload
terms.definition: What a rocket carries for the mission: satellites, a crewed spacecraft, cargo or instruments.

terms.name: perigee
terms.definition: The point of an orbit around Earth that is closest to Earth.
